title: Circumference and Area of Circles
seo_title: Year 8 Circles Worksheets: Circumference, Area, Semicircles and π (Free, Answer Key)
standard_text: solve problems involving the circumference and area of a circle using formulas and appropriate units
meta_desc: Free Year 8 maths worksheets on circles for the Australian Curriculum (AC9M8M03): circumference and area to 1 decimal place and in terms of π, semicircles, quarter circles, finding the radius and real-life problems. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_sub: Always use the radius for the area. Halve the diameter first if you need to.
body_html:
How it works

The radius r goes from the centre to the edge; the diameter d = 2r goes right across.

  • Circumference: C = πd or C = 2πr
  • Area: A = πr² (always use the radius)

Use the π button on a calculator and round at the end, or give an exact answer “in terms of π”, such as 25π.

Example

Find the circumference of a circle with diameter 8 cm.

π × 8 = 25.13…

Answer: 25.1 cm

Example

Find the area of a circle with diameter 8 cm.

Radius = 4 cm.

π × 4² = 16π = 50.26…

Answer: 50.3 cm²

Common mistakes

  • Using the diameter in πr²: with d = 8, the area is π × 4², not π × 8².
  • Mixing up the formulae: 2πr is the circumference, πr² is the area.
  • Squaring π × r instead of just r.
  • For a semicircle's perimeter, forgetting to add the straight diameter.

faq.q: What is the formula for the circumference of a circle?
faq.a: C = πd, or C = 2πr, where d is the diameter and r is the radius.

faq.q: What is the formula for the area of a circle?
faq.a: A = πr². Square the radius first, then multiply by π.

faq.q: What does “in terms of π” mean?
faq.a: Leave π as a symbol instead of using its decimal value. A circle with radius 5 has area 25π cm².

faq.q: How do I find the perimeter of a semicircle?
faq.a: Half of πd for the curved part, plus the diameter for the straight edge.
